test_title: PYST 3: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 26 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the primary goal of the Jal Jeevan Mission?

options.text: Providing piped drinking water to households

solution:
The correct answer is __**Providing piped drinking water to households**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)** is a flagship program of the **Government of India**, launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **August 15, 2019**, during the **73rd Independence Day** speech.

• The primary goal of the mission is to provide **Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC)** to every rural household in the country by the year **2024**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

• The mission ensures the supply of **55 liters of water per capita per day (lpcd)** of prescribed quality (as per **BIS:10500** standards) on a regular and long-term basis.

• **River conservation** is primarily managed under the **Namami Gange Programme** and the **National River Conservation Plan (NRCP)**, rather than the Jal Jeevan Mission. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• **Irrigation system modernization** is the core objective of the **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)**, which aims to improve on-farm water use efficiency. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• While **groundwater recharge** is a component of source sustainability within JJM, it is the primary focus of the **Atal Bhujal Yojana**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Jal Jeevan Mission** is implemented by the **Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation** under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.

• The funding pattern for the mission is shared between the **Centre** and **States** in the ratio of **90:10** for **Himalayan and North-Eastern States**, **50:50** for other states, and **100%** for **Union Territories**.

• **Goa** became the first **Har Ghar Jal** state in **India** by providing **100%** tap water connections to all rural households, followed by **Telangana** and **Haryana**.

• **Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu** became the first **Har Ghar Jal** Union Territory in the country.

• The mission also focuses on **integrated demand and supply-side management** of water at the local level, including **rainwater harvesting** and **greywater management** (domestic wastewater treatment for reuse in agriculture).

**Important Points__**

• The mission is a **community-led movement** involving **Panchayati Raj Institutions** and **Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSC)**, often referred to as **Pani Samitis**, which play a key role in planning, implementation, and management.

• In **2021**, the **Jal Jeevan Mission (Urban)** was launched to provide universal coverage of water supply through functional taps in all **4,378 Statutory Towns**, aligning with **Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6)**.

• The program emphasizes **Water Quality Monitoring and Surveillance (WQMS)**, encouraging the use of **Field Test Kits (FTKs)** by community members, especially women, to test water samples for contamination.

• As of **2023-2024**, the mission has significantly increased rural tap water coverage from approximately **17%** in **2019** to over **75%** nationwide, showcasing rapid infrastructure development.

• The **Jal Jeevan Survekshan** is an annual assessment conducted to rank districts and states based on their performance in implementing the mission goals.
